name: Two-pole one-way switch plan mark
summary: Plan mark for a one-way switch that breaks both line and neutral, drawn with two ticks on the stroke.
description: A two-pole one-way switch opens both poles of a single-phase circuit. The IEC plan convention adds a second tick to the one-way switch stroke, giving the reader an immediate visual cue that the switch interrupts both conductors.

Two-pole switches are specified for outdoor lighting, appliances where both poles must be broken, and some heating loads. They are also used where a switch is expected to provide functional disconnection of a fixed appliance without a separate isolator.
Two ticks do not mean the switch meets isolation requirements for maintenance. Where isolation is needed, the designer should show an isolator mark or state the isolating rating.
readingNotes: Count the ticks carefully when the drawing is reduced in size.
Check whether a separate isolator is also shown for the same load.
drawingChecklist: State whether isolation duty is intended.
Confirm current rating for heating or appliance loads.
distinction: The single-tick one-way switch breaks one pole only; the two-tick form breaks both.
